summary:
George Hill (1750–1819) was a Scottish minister and academic who became a leading figure in the Church of Scotland’s Moderate party. Born in St Andrews, he graduated from its university at 14 and later taught Greek and divinity there. He served as a minister in St Andrews, became principal of St Mary’s College, and held senior church posts.

Hill was Moderator of the General Assembly in 1789 and succeeded William Robertson as leader of the Moderates. He supported compromise over church patronage but firmly defended the Church’s independence from government. He also opposed political campaigning from pulpits.

A founding member of the Royal Society of Edinburgh in 1783, Hill remained active in church and university life until illness curtailed his work. He died in St Andrews on 19 November 1819 and was buried near its cathedral.
